posts.title: When Technology Becomes a Tool of Abuse
posts.standfirst: Online abuse can follow people into their homes, relationships, workplaces and public lives. Understanding technology-facilitated gender-based violence is the first step towards responding properly.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Young women at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: A Peaceful Election Is Not Always a Safe Election for Women
posts.standfirst: Women’s political participation carries costs that men do not always bear in the same way. If Nigeria wants safer elections, it must look beyond polling-day calm and confront the threats, reputational attacks and institutional failures that push women out of public life.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Women listening at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: The Fight Against Gender-Based Violence Starts Long Before the First Blow
posts.standfirst: Gender-based violence often becomes visible only after harm has already taken hold. Prevention begins earlier, by helping communities recognise abuse, challenge the norms that excuse it, and build trusted systems that make safer choices possible.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Men and young people at a BBYDI community townhall on gender-based violence

posts.title: Nigeria already knows how to make schools safer. It keeps buying something else
posts.standfirst: Nigeria issued a national school safety policy in 2021. Five years on, states are still forming committees, and the threat map that policy was built for no longer matches where children are being taken.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Secondary school students gathered for a BBYDI climate education session

posts.title: Online abuse, offline silence
posts.standfirst: The response to online gender-based violence focuses on platforms and moderation, and it should. But the harm also happens in an offline world of family and community, where old norms decide whether a woman is believed or blamed, and moderation cannot follow her there.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Young women at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: The men who thought not hitting their wives was enough
posts.standfirst: Preventing gender-based violence means reaching the men who believe they are already part of the solution, and funding the slow work of changing what a community accepts as normal.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Traditional and religious leaders at BBYDI’s high-level statewide event against gender-based violence in Kwara State

posts.title: This June 12, Nigeria’s Democracy Faces a Threat It Has Never Seen
posts.standfirst: In 1993, the men who ran Nigeria buried the result of its freest election. Ahead of the 2027 vote, the danger is harder to fight: AI-generated fakes that take seconds to make and are already spreading online.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Panel and youth artwork at the BBYDI Youth Artivism Festival on GBV prevention

posts.title: Nigeria Knows the Floods Are Coming. The Question Is Whether Communities Will Hear the Warning in Time
posts.standfirst: NiMet and NIHSA can now predict where the floods will hit. The unfinished work is making sure the warnings reach the people they are meant for in time, in their language, and from voices they trust.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Secondary school students gathered for a BBYDI climate education session

posts.title: What 1,423 essays revealed about how Nigerian students are using AI
posts.standfirst: In a national competition about responsible AI use, the commonest reason an essay missed the shortlist was that the student had leaned too hard on AI to write it.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Students working together at the BBYDI-PJMF national essay competition grand finale

posts.title: How to Check a WhatsApp Message Before You Share It
posts.standfirst: A message lands in your group claiming exams are cancelled or an outbreak has reached your area. Your instinct is to forward it. Five steps to check first.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Participants holding placards at the BBYDI-PJMF AI literacy training for parents, communities and youths

posts.title: Five Things We Got Wrong About Community Dialogue on GBV And What We Changed
posts.standfirst: We planned community dialogues on gender-based violence in Kwara State. Most of our assumptions didn’t survive the first session.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Men and young people at a BBYDI community townhall on gender-based violence

posts.title: What 93 Nigerian Teachers Discovered About AI in a Single Day
posts.standfirst: Hands-on workshops in Kwara and Osun states found that teachers weren’t reluctant to use AI, they just hadn’t been shown what it could do.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Participants holding placards at the BBYDI-PJMF AI literacy training for parents, communities and youths

posts.title: When Citizens Understand The Budget, They Demand Accountability
posts.standfirst: Market traders in Kwara long heard about budgets on the news without knowing what they meant for the markets. After budget literacy training they are asking questions.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Men and young people at a BBYDI community townhall on gender-based violence

posts.title: AI Literacy Must Be Built Locally — Or It Will Leave Most Nigerians Behind
posts.standfirst: The global push for AI education was not designed with Nigerian realities in mind. It shows.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Participants holding placards at the BBYDI-PJMF AI literacy training for parents, communities and youths

posts.title: She Reported It on WhatsApp: How KEMI Is Reaching Women Where Other Services Can’t
posts.standfirst: An AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot, co-designed with survivors, is connecting women facing online violence to real support in under a minute.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Young women at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: The Flood That Climate Change Didn’t Cause Alone
posts.standfirst: In Mokwa, Nigeria, a deadly storm met a broken system and the result was devastating.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Secondary school students gathered for a BBYDI climate education session

posts.title: Bruised and Blamed: What It Means to Be a Woman in Nigeria Today
posts.standfirst: She was not killed in a war, but her body carried the signs of one. For millions of Nigerian women, home is the battleground and justice a distant rumour.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Women listening at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: ‘I Used Ashes Instead of Pads’: The Hidden Crisis of Menstrual Health in Nigeria
posts.standfirst: Every month girls across Nigeria vanish from classrooms because they are menstruating, improvising with rags, old newspapers or ashes.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: BBYDI team and Padded Girls participants with a community leader at the project close-out

posts.title: She Thought It Was Just a Visit. This Is What Tech-Facilitated Violence Looks Like
posts.standfirst: We talk about safety. We talk about girls. But we don’t talk about how the internet has become the perfect place to make them disappear.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Young women at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: Killed for Being Women: Unmasking the Femicide Crisis in Nigeria
posts.standfirst: Most Nigerian femicides are never named as such. They are buried inside generic homicide statistics, which is part of why so little changes.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Women listening at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence

posts.title: From Waste to Wealth: How Nigeria Can Lead in Sustainable Fashion
posts.standfirst: Katangua market swallows the world’s cast-off clothing. A few Nigerian designers are building the opposite — a fashion economy that treats waste as raw material.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Students at a BBYDI climate education session in school

posts.title: YouthGovTracka: Holding State Governors Accountable for Youth-Inclusive Policies
posts.standfirst: Campaign promises are central to elections yet often abandoned in office. YouthGovTracka tracks and evaluates governors’ youth commitments, showing who is delivering and who is falling short.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: BBYDI staff at the Abuja launch of their civic engagement research

posts.title: How MyAIFactChecker is Using AI to Combat Misinformation in Africa
posts.standfirst: Misinformation across Africa threatens economies, political outcomes and public health. MyAIFactChecker analyses both the factual content and the sentiment of a claim, in seven African languages.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Participants holding placards at the BBYDI-PJMF AI literacy training for parents, communities and youths

posts.title: Padded Girls: Training Women on Reusable Pads to Ease Period Poverty
posts.standfirst: More than 300 million women menstruate on any given day, and in rural Kwara the cost of pads decides who stays in the classroom. The Padded Girls Project trained women to make their own.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: BBYDI team and Padded Girls participants at the project close-out

posts.title: #SpaceForHer: Increasing Female Participation in Politics and Promoting Gender Inclusion
posts.standfirst: In the 2023 elections only 8.6% of senatorial candidates were women. The six-week SpaceForHer residency fellowship set out to change that.
posts.heroFallbackAlt: Women listening at a BBYDI community townhall on technology-facilitated gender-based violence
